title: Kong API Gateway 3.16 adds entitlement enforcement and live operations controls
summary: Kong API Gateway 3.16 adds OpenMeter-powered request-time entitlement enforcement for usage limits and plan-based feature access, plus runtime log-level changes and per-principal plugin configuration. Kong's release blog also describes prepaid-credit enforcement, but the current 3.16 documentation explicitly says credit-balance enforcement is not implemented yet. The release strengthens Kong's monetization and enterprise-governance platform, but no adoption or financial contribution is disclosed, so the score and valuation model are unchanged.
confirmed: Kong released API Gateway 3.16 on September 22, 2026.

Kong's Entitlement Enforcement documentation says the plugin can block requests when a customer reaches a usage limit or lacks access to a boolean feature, and it works alongside the separately purchased Metering & Billing product.

Kong's current 3.16 documentation states that credit-balance enforcement is not implemented: config.credit_balance_required and the NO_CREDIT_AVAILABLE reason code are present in the schema but currently have no effect.

Administrators can change log verbosity at runtime on Hybrid Data Planes, and selected ACL and rate-limiting plugin fields can now vary per request using Common Expression Language expressions based on principal, consumer, and token-claim data.
The release also includes a separately distributed FIPS 140-3-compliant package, overlapping Kong's previously recorded September 3 FIPS announcement.
uncertain: Kong did not disclose customer adoption, pricing, attach rates, bookings, ARR, retention, gross-margin, or free-cash-flow impact for Gateway 3.16 or the Entitlement Enforcement plugin.
Kong has not stated when credit-balance enforcement will become functional.
Because OpenMeter acquisition and Konnect Metering & Billing evidence were already recorded, the commercial benefit should not be counted again until usage or revenue evidence appears.
